issues.legal_issue: An appellate court may not substitute its view for a reasoned exercise of discretion on an application for temporary injunction unless that discretion was exercised arbitrarily, perversely, or contrary to settled principles.
material_facts: The trial court refused the principal request for a temporary injunction after considering the pleadings and evidence and giving reasons concerning the claimed mark, likely confusion, and the balance of equities.
The appellate court substantially agreed with the trial court’s findings, and the Supreme Court found those findings to be based on a balanced consideration of the material.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court found no basis to interfere with the appellate court’s refusal to grant the principal temporary injunction.
issues.legal_principle: Under Wander Ltd. v. Antox India (P) Ltd., an appeal from the exercise of discretion on an interlocutory injunction is an appeal on principle; an appellate court should not reassess the material merely to reach a different view where the decision below was reasonably possible. The approach was reiterated in N.R. Dongre v. Whirlpool Corporation and considered consistently with Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals. Interference is warranted where discretion was exercised arbitrarily, capriciously, or perversely, or settled principles governing interlocutory injunctions were ignored.

rule.if: appeal_challenges_interlocutory_injunction_discretion and lower_court_gave_cogent_reasons and decision_was_reasonably_possible and not discretion_was_arbitrary_perverse_or_unprincipled

predicates.appeal_challenges_interlocutory_injuncti: The appeal challenges a court’s exercise of discretion on an application for temporary injunction.
predicates.lower_court_gave_cogent_reasons: The lower court considered the material and gave reasons for its decision on temporary relief.
predicates.decision_was_reasonably_possible: The conclusion reached by the lower court was reasonably open on the material before it.
predicates.discretion_was_arbitrary_perverse_or_unp: The lower court exercised its discretion arbitrarily or perversely, or ignored settled principles governing temporary injunctions.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges interlocutory injunction discretion, a reasoned decision that was reasonably possible is left undisturbed unless the discretion was arbitrary, perverse, or unprincipled.

issues.legal_issue: A prior user who seeks an interim injunction against another user of a widely used name must establish a prima facie basis for restraining that use, and the relief remains subject to equitable considerations.
material_facts: The appellant relied principally on its prior use of the word in the education field and claimed that the later use would cause confusion and harm its goodwill.
The word was used by numerous businesses and institutions, including educational institutions, as part of their names.

The appellant’s applications for registration had been pending when the interim relief was considered; registration obtained during the suit did not, by itself, establish entitlement to the requested injunction.

The respondents had obtained relevant recognition and affiliation, admitted students, and made substantial investments in establishing their institution, while the appellant lacked comparable statutory approval or university affiliation.
The courts below found that the appellant had not made out a prima facie case and that the balance of convenience and equity did not support the requested restraint.
issues.conclusion: The refusal to restrain use of the word as part of the respondents’ institutional name was upheld, and the later registration alone did not justify interim relief.
issues.legal_principle: An unregistered prior user may bring a passing-off action, but must establish that the defendant misrepresented its services as those of the claimant and that the misrepresentation harmed the claimant’s goodwill or reputation, or caused loss. A temporary injunction is equitable and depends on the prima facie case, balance of convenience, irreparable injury, and equity. The Court applied the appellate-interference principles in Wander Ltd. v. Antox India (P) Ltd. and N.R. Dongre v. Whirlpool Corporation, and referred to Cadila Health Care Ltd. v. Cadila Pharmaceuticals in that context. Registration obtained during the suit, without more, did not establish entitlement to the requested interim restraint.

predicates.application_seeks_temporary_name_use_res: A party seeks temporary relief preventing another party from using a name in connection with its activities.
predicates.name_is_widely_used_by_other_businesses_: The name is used by numerous other businesses or institutions, including in the relevant field.
predicates.prima_facie_misrepresentation_and_harm_s: The claimant has shown a prima facie case that the other party misrepresented its services as the claimant’s and thereby harmed the claimant’s goodwill or caused loss.
predicates.equitable_factors_do_not_favour_restrain: The circumstances, including the parties’ approvals, investments, existing operations, and the balance of convenience, do not favour restraining the other party.

issues.definition: A temporary restraint on name use is refused where the name is widely used, a prima facie case of harmful misrepresentation is absent, and the equitable circumstances do not favour restraint.

issues.legal_issue: When an appellate court concludes that the directions in an interim injunction were unjustified, it should remove those directions rather than leave any part of that injunction in force.
material_facts: The trial court had restrained the respondents from starting specified courses and required them to include a disclaimer in advertisements.

The appellate court held that those directions were unjustified because the appellant had failed to establish the basis for an injunction, but did not set aside the trial court’s directions in their entirety.
The Supreme Court allowed the respondents’ appeal and vacated the modified injunction in its entirety.
issues.conclusion: The remaining directions were set aside, and the modified injunction was vacated in its entirety.
issues.legal_principle: Where an appellate court determines that the trial court ought not to have issued the challenged injunctive directions, it should set aside the injunction in its entirety; leaving the directions partly operative calls for corrective action.

predicates.appeal_challenges_remaining_interim_inju: An appeal challenges directions that remain in an interim injunction.
predicates.appellate_court_finds_the_directions_unj: The appellate court concludes that the challenged injunctive directions should not have been issued.
predicates.some_directions_remain_in_force: Despite that conclusion, one or more of the challenged directions remain operative.

issues.definition: When an appeal concerns remaining interim injunction directions that the appellate court has found unjustified, any directions still in force are removed by setting aside the injunction in its entirety.
